title: Those of you that use AI to generate 3D models, how do you make your prompt better?
author: Full-Principle7054
selftext: I've been experimenting with some text to image to 3d tools like Meshy and trellis but I think my prompts aren't good enough the models look off sometimes. What prompt tweaks work for you?

replies.author: Savings-Singer-1202
replies.body: you're confusing raw density with quality topology. 1.5M vertices from an AI generator is usually 'point cloud soup' it lacks edge loops for deformation, has terrible UV islands, and kills the frame rate due to unnecessary draw calls. In a real-time pipeline, we want the lowest vertex count possible that still holds the silhouette, while using those 1.5M vertices only for baking Normal and AO maps onto a clean, retopologized mesh. High vertex count without optimization isn't 'information,' it's just technical debt.

comments.author: PhysicalServe3399
comments.body: Hey! I've been working on a project called [magicshot.ai](https://magicshot.ai) that also focuses on generating 3D assets from AI-generated images. One thing that really helps is being super specific with your prompts, describe not just the object, but also the material, lighting, and style (e.g., “low-poly,” “realistic,” or “game-ready”). If you're interested, feel free to check out MagicShot—it's my project, and I'm always open to feedback!

comments.author: Particular_Lack2817
comments.body:
Here's how you can get better results : 

Upgrade your guidance for model generation  
\- With only prompt : use reference images for 1) style and 2) model reference, and ask AI to get appropriate description of these images for prompt generation  
\- With 2D images for references : some of these tools can have image inputs. It drives AI toward better results, don't hesitate  

Then **you refine** what you just got generatedIf you are unsatisfied with what has been generated, let's say 90% is fine, don't start again from scratch.   
Build from 90% to reach 100%. For that, you can use modddif .com  
The app let you generate from scratch and then refine your model in an iterative process. It's still an early product but already it has tremendous features

comments.author: IfnotFr
comments.body: Try imagining you’re describing your dream sculpture to a robot artist with zero imagination, be absurdly precise. Like “a shiny bronze dragon curled around a neon pink cube, under moonlight with soft shadows.” Vivid, unusual combos help AI nail the shape.

comments.author: Zorya0134
comments.body: I usually use Gemini or ChatGPT to help me work on better prompts. I just describe what I’m aiming for and ask them to give me a few versions to try. It works pretty well, though sometimes it feels like a lot of back and forth 😅I also use meshy and trellis, meshy’s built-in prompt help can be useful too, especially when I don’t want to overthink it. But yeah, I totally agree that AI tools still struggle with things like textures or properly mapped materials.

comments.author: Overall-Cry9838
comments.body:
honestly i think the best workflow now is not pure text to 3d anymore, but image generation/editing first and then image to 3d afterwards.

what works way better for me is:

1. first generate the concept image
2. edit/refine the image until the design is exactly what you want
3. generate side/back views if needed
4. then run image to 3d or multi image to 3d

that gives way more control over the final result.

for example, i’ll often first generate the concept with something like nano banana pro, imagen4, or flux locally. then i edit the image until the silhouette/style/details are correct before even touching 3d generation.

that step is super underrated because you can:

*change the style*  
*remove objects*  
*add details*  
*fix proportions*  
*generate cleaner front/side/back views*

and all of that massively improves the final 3d result.

a lot of bad image to 3d outputs actually come from bad source images, not necessarily bad 3d models.

tool wise, i’d probably start with 3daistudio for this workflow because it already combines image gen/editing with image to 3d, multi image to 3d, remeshing, textures, etc in one place. tripo 3.1 ultra mesh can give pretty solid meshes, meshy is also popular, but honestly the quality of the input images matters more than people think.

honestly wouldt do text to 3d at all anymore, hope that helped!! : )
